binders: A type Ω equipped with a measurable-space structure.
A measure μ on Ω equipped with a probability-measure instance.
A real-valued function X : Ω → Real.
hypotheses: X is pointwise nonnegative: for every ω ∈ Ω, 0 ≤ X(ω).
conclusions: The nonnegative extended-real integral of ENNReal.ofReal(X) with respect to μ equals the nonnegative extended-real integral, over positive real thresholds t with respect to restricted real-line volume, of μ({ω ∈ Ω | t < X(ω)}).

If X is integrable with respect to μ, then its real-valued integral ∫ X dμ equals the real-valued integral, over positive real thresholds t with respect to restricted real-line volume, of the real value of μ({ω ∈ Ω | t < X(ω)}).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 μ X means the real-valued integral ∫ X dμ.
The threshold event at t is the strict superlevel set {ω ∈ Ω | t < X(ω)}.
The threshold-integration measure is standard real-line volume restricted to the open positive half-line (0,∞).
In the first identity, superlevel-set measures are ENNReal-valued; in the second, μ.real converts them to real values.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For a measurable nonnegative real-valued random variable on a probability space, its nonnegative extended expectation is the integral over all positive thresholds of the probability that the variable exceeds the threshold. If the variable is integrable, the corresponding identity also holds as an ordinary real-valued integral.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The measure is explicitly required to be a probability measure, even though the displayed identities may be meaningful under weaker measure assumptions.
Nonnegativity is pointwise for every ω, not merely almost everywhere.
The second equality is guarded by an integrability implication; when X is not integrable, that component imposes no equality and is logically vacuous.
The first equality remains asserted without an integrability hypothesis and may take the value ∞ on either side.
The threshold sets use strict inequality t < X(ω), and thresholds are integrated only over the open interval (0,∞).
The notation μ.real uses ENNReal.toReal; under the integrability premise, the relevant superlevel-set values are finite in the probability-measure setting.
